title: Grade 12 MUSIC AND DANCE — General Assessment #5

pages.quiz:
MUSIC AND DANCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #5
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: MUSIC AND DANCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Warming up before sport helps to: (1 mark)
   A. Replace drinking water
   B. Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk
   C. Guarantee a trophy
   D. Remove the need for rules

2. Best practice when working on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   B. Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Damage equipment used for Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World.

3. Best practice when working on Setting Text to Music: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Setting Text to Music.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Setting Text to Music.
   C. Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Setting Text to Music.

4. Best practice when working on Music Notation Software.: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Music Notation Software..
   C. Disrupt classmates during Music Notation Software..
   D. Damage equipment used for Music Notation Software..

5. Best practice when working on Four-Part Harmony: (1 mark)
   A. Disrupt classmates during Four-Part Harmony.
   B. Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Four-Part Harmony.
   D. Damage equipment used for Four-Part Harmony.

6. Best practice when working on Kenyan Contemporary Songs: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   B. Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan Contemporary Songs.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan Contemporary Songs.

7. Best practice when working on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble: (1 mark)
   A. Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   B. Refuse all feedback on Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   C. Disrupt classmates during Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.
   D. Damage equipment used for Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble.

8. Primary colours are: (1 mark)
   A. Red, blue, and yellow
   B. Green, orange, and purple
   C. Black, white, and grey
   D. Brown, pink, and gold

9. Best practice when working on Rhythm: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Rhythm.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Rhythm.
   C. Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Refuse all feedback on Rhythm.

10. In music, tempo refers to: (1 mark)
   A. Only the volume
   B. The speed of the music
   C. Only the costume
   D. The ticket price

11. Best practice when working on Western Ensembles: (1 mark)
   A. Refuse all feedback on Western Ensembles.
   B. Disrupt classmates during Western Ensembles.
   C. Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   D. Damage equipment used for Western Ensembles.

12. Best practice when working on Instrumental Transpositions: (1 mark)
   A. Damage equipment used for Instrumental Transpositions.
   B. Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.
   C. Refuse all feedback on Instrumental Transpositions.
   D. Disrupt classmates during Instrumental Transpositions.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Classical Music and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Music and Dance Industry and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Rhythm and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Instrumental Transpositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Prepare muscles and reduce injury risk

2. B — Practise Contemporary Dances from the Rest of the World with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

3. C — Practise Setting Text to Music with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

4. A — Practise Music Notation Software. with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

5. B — Practise Four-Part Harmony with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

6. B — Practise Kenyan Contemporary Songs with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

7. A — Practise Kenyan -Western Instrumental Ensemble with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

8. A — Red, blue, and yellow

9. C — Practise Rhythm with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

10. B — The speed of the music

11. C — Practise Western Ensembles with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

12. B — Practise Instrumental Transpositions with discipline, creativity, and respect for others.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Classical Music; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Music and Dance Industry; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Rhythm; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Instrumental Transpositions; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
